# rd_filters structural alert collection (Walters)

1,251 SMARTS alerts assembled from eight published medicinal-chemistry filter sets -- BMS, Dundee, Glaxo, Inpharmatica, LINT, MLSMR, PAINS and SureChEMBL -- each carrying the occurrence count above which it fires.

- Walters, W. P. rd_filters: filter compounds using RDKit and a set of structural alerts. GitHub: PatWalters/rd_filters 2018.
  - https://github.com/PatWalters/rd_filters
  - The tool itself has no paper. The alert sets it collects are published separately and are cited below.
- Baell, J. B.; Holloway, G. A. New Substructure Filters for Removal of Pan Assay Interference Compounds (PAINS) from Screening Libraries and for Their Exclusion in Bioassays. Journal of Medicinal Chemistry 53(7), 2719-2740 2010. DOI: 10.1021/jm901137j
  - https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/jm901137j
  - Source of the 481 PAINS rules.
- Bruns, R. F.; Watson, I. A. Evaluating the Utility of Compound Filters: Lessons from a Large-Scale Analysis. Journal of Medicinal Chemistry 55(22), 9763-9772 2012. DOI: 10.1021/jm301008n
  - https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/jm301008n
  - Source of the BMS ('Bruns-Watson') rule set.
- Rishton, G. M.; Hann, M. M.; and the Glaxo Wellcome group. A Knowledge-Based Approach in Designing Combinatorial or Medicinal Chemistry Libraries for Drug Discovery. Journal of Combinatorial Chemistry 1(1), 55-68 1999. DOI: 10.1021/cc9800071
  - https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/cc9800071
  - Source of the Glaxo 'hard filters'. Reported by Hann et al.; the Dundee and SureChEMBL sets derive from the same tradition of reactive-group and unwanted-chemistry lists.

## Referencing these files from a cascade

Use an `asset:` reference so the configuration means the same thing on every machine:

```
asset:rd_filters/data/alert_collection.csv
asset:rd_filters/data/rules.json
asset:rd_filters/LICENSE
asset:rd_filters/rd_filters.py
```

## Notes

MolCascade reads the CSV and compiles each SMARTS into an RDKit `FilterCatalog` entry whose minimum match count is `max + 1`, which is the same test the upstream script applies (`len(GetSubstructMatches) > max`). It differs from upstream in one deliberate way: upstream stops at the first matching rule and returns a single string, while MolCascade reports every rule set that matched and lets each set carry its own ignore/warn/reject action, so PAINS can warn while a reactive-group set rejects.

An alert is a substructure match, not experimental evidence. Baell and Walters have both written at length about over-applying these lists; the adapter therefore defaults every set to `warn` except the reactive-chemistry sets, and never silently deletes a molecule without recording the rule that removed it.

---

This file is generated by `molcascade assets fetch`. MolCascade downloads nothing during a screening run; if a file listed above is absent or its digest disagrees, the backend that needs it stops rather than proceeding.
